extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated entities, and stakeholders who monitor Department of Labor Federal Register notices and who may submit comments or respond to information collection requests
extracted.subtask_description: A listing of Department of Labor Federal Register documents (notices, proposed rules, final rules) that publish information collection requests, privacy-act system-of-records notices, exemptions, meeting notices, and corrections—documents that invite public comment or otherwise notify stakeholders of agency actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) pre-clearance consultation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Labor, as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, conducts a pre-clearance consultation program for all information collections, to provide the public and Federal agencies with an opportunity to comment on proposed collections of information, in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose and expected outcomes stated repeatedly: help ensure requested data can be provided in the desired format; reporting burden (time and financial resources) is minimized; collection instruments are clearly understood; and the impact of collection requirements on respondents can be properly assessed. Notices should invite public comments and provide contact information for obtaining copies of proposed ICRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Collection Request (ICR) submission and OMB review/approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies submit ICRs to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval in accordance with the PRA; public comments on the ICR are invited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must state that the ICR is submitted for OMB review/approval, invite public comment, and provide instructions for obtaining the proposed ICR (typically by contacting the individual listed in the ADDRESSES section). Extensions of previously approved ICRs (e.g., OMB approval renewal/extension) are published with solicitations for comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of public comments for OMB approval extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA (and other DOL components) publishes notices soliciting public comments concerning proposals to extend OMB approval of the information collection requirements specified in particular standards (e.g., HAZWOPER, EtO Standard, Fire Brigades Standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such notices should identify the standard whose ICR approval is proposed for extension, explain that comments are solicited on the extension proposal, and provide links or instructions for accessing the full notice/ICR for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act / System of Records notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Privacy Act of 1974 and OMB Circular No. A-108 require that each agency publish notice of a new or modified system of records that it maintains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modifying a system of records, agencies must publish a notice describing changes (e.g., adding a new routine use). Notices should reference relevant Executive Orders and OMB memoranda (for example, Executive Order 14249; OMB Memoranda M-25-32 and M-17-12) when adding routine uses such as disclosures to Treasury or model routine uses permitting disclosure in response to a breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and access to proposed collection materials
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the proposed information collection request (ICR) can be obtained by contacting the individual listed in the ADDRESSES section of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices should include explicit instructions for how interested parties can obtain proposed collection instruments and supporting documentation (contacts, addresses, links to PDFs), facilitating informed public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of corrections to prior Federal Register notices
rubrics_metrics.description: When an earlier Federal Register notice contains an error (e.g., incorrect RIN citation), agencies publish a correction notice to fix the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction notices should identify the original notice (date and specific error), explain the mistake, and state the correct information. Corrections ensure clarity for stakeholders relying on prior notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement of advisory committee meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies publish notices announcing advisory committee meetings (e.g., ACCSH virtual meeting dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting notices should provide dates, format (virtual/in-person), and any procedural details required for public participation or observation, so stakeholders can attend or submit input as allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of final rule actions (including revocations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies publish final rules to announce actions such as the revocation of an existing regulatory standard (e.g., revocation of the Open Fires in Marine Terminals Standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule notices should state the agency action (adoption, amendment, or revocation), the rationale or summary of the decision, effective dates, and citations to the affected regulations so regulated parties understand the change and compliance implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional exemptions and eligibility notices (Prohibited Transaction Exemptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices may grant exemptions (for example, allowing UBS-related asset managers to rely on PTE 84-14 from May 5, 2026 to May 5, 2035) provided certain conditions are met, notwithstanding related convictions or agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption notices should specify the scope and duration of the exemption, the conditions that must be met for reliance, and any limitations or contextual facts (such as convictions or non-prosecution agreements) relevant to the exemption.
